cadence: Weekly news picks, refreshed every Monday alongside citation rankings.
selection: The top stories from the trailing 30 days, scored on publisher authority, discussion volume, whether a concrete verifiable result is reported, whether it changes what agent builders do now, whether an artifact was released, and expected durability. Only primary sources are cited, and performance claims remain attributed to their publishers.

items.source: Stanford / Tel Aviv University et al. · arXiv
items.title: Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data
items.why: The authors train a program generator and byte-sequence learner from random initialization, using self-play to create a curriculum. They report predictable zero-shot loss scaling on natural datasets without natural-data gradient updates. Natural validation data still guide hyperparameter selection, and the result is a proof of concept.

items.source: SJTU / Theseus Labs / Tencent Hunyuan · arXiv
items.title: Breaking the Environment Wall: Evolving LLM Agent Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.why: The authors introduce Env-Rethink, a system with a 27B post-trained model that organizes context, diagnoses environmental noise and generates harder environments through virtual event histories. They report improved rubric pass rates across nine downstream models on 30 tasks.

items.source: ELLIS / MPI-IS / Snyk et al. · arXiv
items.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
items.why: The authors find that tested local coding harnesses, except Muse Code, allow agents to delete their own execution traces when prompted, without triggering monitor guardrails. They also demonstrate externally induced and reward-driven trace tampering, motivating logging outside the agent-controlled environment.

items.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
items.why: OpenAI reports 68.8% for Sol and 66.6% for Luna on DeepSWE v1.1 at max effort, and introduces lower token prices and cache controls for long-running agents.

items.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5
items.why: Anthropic reports 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at xhigh effort and says lower token prices and token usage reduce costs by 40% versus Opus 5. The published evaluations use production safeguards and disclosed fallback models.

items.title: Introducing Grok 4.7
items.why: SpaceXAI says Grok 4.7 uses a larger base model and longer reinforcement learning on multi-hour tasks. It reports 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6, with unchanged starting token prices.

items.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
items.why: The authors regularize harness edits and selection to reduce benchmark-specific overfitting. Across eight benchmarks, they report gains up to 4.7 points on five out-of-distribution benchmarks and 30% fewer policy tokens than unregularized evolution, with code released.

items.title: Introducing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2: Orchestrating the Pareto Frontier
items.why: Sakana AI releases Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2 around a shared orchestration architecture, expanding the pool of open-weight and specialized models. It argues that routing tasks to appropriate models improves the capability-cost frontier.

items.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Smarter, Faster, More Efficient
items.why: DeepSeek releases a 552B MoE with a causal encoder-decoder architecture activating 8B parameters on input and 16B on output. It says the KV cache needs one quarter of the prior generation's HBM, and links model weights and a technical report.

items.title: Introducing SWE-2: Pushing the Pareto Frontier
items.why: Cognition post-trains the 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 base with an RL algorithm covering all reasoning-effort levels in one run. It reports 50.0% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main at 64% lower cost than Fable 5.1.
